info.title: Tari Public Data API
info.description:
Programmatic access to Tari WMS data — items, vendors, bundles, purchase orders, cargo loads, marketing campaigns, product reviews, SKU stock coverage, and ocean cargo tracking. Read is the bulk of the surface; a growing set of scoped WRITE operations covers inventory documents (receipts / issues / adjustments / transfers), master data (items / vendors, including create / update / delete), purchasing (purchase order create / update), and logistics (cargo load create / update / depart). FK / code lookup endpoints (facilities, payment terms, categories) resolve the ids and codes the write bodies take.

## Authentication

Every request requires a per-app bearer token, sent in the `Authorization` header:

`Authorization: Bearer <token>`

Generate and manage tokens in the Tari console under **System → API tokens** (`/console/settings/api-tokens`). The key is shown **only once** at creation — store it securely. If a key is lost or leaked, revoke it and issue a new one. Tokens do not expire; revoking is the only way to retire one. A missing, invalid, or revoked token returns `401`.

A second auth axis — warehouse **worker sessions** (Supabase Auth JWT, so a write attributes to the acting worker) — is designed but not yet live; operations that will accept it are annotated with an **Auth axis** note.

## Pagination

Results use keyset pagination. Each response includes a `next_cursor`; pass it back as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. A `null` `next_cursor` means you have reached the last page. Set page size with `limit` (default 100, max 500).

## Rate limits

Each token is limited to 5 requests per second (burst) and 100 requests per minute.

## Excluded fields

Most datasets minimize sensitive fields, but this is dataset-specific rather than blanket: items expose cost/price (internal consumers), and the vendors dataset intentionally exposes contact + address PII (WOO-541 — the token is an internal-org credential). Provenance / external-link fields (external_id, drive_folder_id) and image assets stay out of the write surface regardless.

## Inventory writes

Inventory is changed through **documents**, never a direct set-quantity call. Post a receipt (stock in), an issue (stock out), an adjustment (count correction), or a transfer (facility-to-facility move) and the system records the ledger. There is no endpoint to overwrite a quantity.

Writes require the `write:inventory` scope (currently granted to every token — internal consumers only; expect per-token gating before any external exposure). Every write also requires an `Idempotency-Key` header: retrying with the same key never double-writes the ledger, and the replay returns `200 { "noop": true }`. A completed receipt/issue writes stock immediately; a draft records the document without touching inventory.

## Master data writes

Items (`POST /items`, `PATCH /items/{id}`, `DELETE /items/{id}`) and vendors (`POST /vendors`, `PATCH /vendors/{id}`, `DELETE /vendors/{id}`) can be created, updated, and soft-deleted. Writes require the `write:masters` scope and an `Idempotency-Key` header (same replay semantics as inventory writes). WOO-541 widened the request bodies: vendors now accept contact / street address / compliance identifiers / note, and items accept trade/customs, shelf life, purchase cost, sales/MD, and packaging fields. Still console-only: `lot_tracking` / `lot_profile` (the INV-007 oversell gate), images, ingredients, and `external_id`. An item’s `sku` is immutable after creation (a sku on PATCH returns 400); barcodes are a declarative full-replace set. DELETE takes no body and is idempotent in effect (a replay hits the already-deleted row → 404). Resolve `category_id` via `GET /categories`.

## Purchasing writes

Purchase orders can be created (`POST /purchase-orders`) and updated (`PATCH /purchase-orders/{id}`) under the `write:purchasing` scope (+ `Idempotency-Key`). A PO is a document — no inventory, charges, or inbound shipment (receiving is a separate flow). Designate the supplier by `supplier_id` and/or `supplier_code`. Edit gating mirrors the console: a draft or an ordered PO whose inbound has not shipped takes full edits; once the inbound is in_transit / partially_received, lines are quantity-only and may only shrink (≥ received); a line on a cargo load can never be deleted. Allowed status transitions: draft→ordered, draft→cancelled, ordered→draft (a revert is blocked when a line is on a cargo load). Resolve `payment_term_code` via `GET /payment-terms` and `destination_facility_id` via `GET /facilities`.

## Logistics writes

Cargo loads (inbound container manifests) can be created (`POST /cargo-loads`), updated (`PATCH /cargo-loads/{id}`), and departed (`POST /cargo-loads/{id}/depart`) — all under the `write:purchasing` scope (+ `Idempotency-Key`). Create / update are document-only (no inventory / receiving); lines reference PO lines by `po_line_id` (see `GET /cargo-loads/available-po-line-items`). **depart** is the one status transition exposed: it approves-then-departs a draft (or departs an approved load), creating the linked inbound shipment and pulling the POs into transit. Everything downstream — arrive and receive — stays in the warehouse flows and is deliberately NOT exposed here.

tags.name: Master data
tags.description: Items, vendors, and bundles — the stable master data exports.

tags.name: Purchasing
tags.description: Purchase orders — header spend rollups, line-level purchase prices, and document create/update (draft-only edits, restricted status transitions).

tags.name: Logistics
tags.description: Cargo loads — inbound container shipments: manifest, schedule (ETD/ETA), and freight/duty charges.

tags.name: Inventory
tags.description: WMS-native inventory — item-grain rollups, per-facility/location/lot detail, and document-based writes (receipts, issues, adjustments, transfers). Authoritative (wms_inventory_levels), unlike the legacy stock-coverage endpoint.

tags.name: Reference
tags.description: FK / code lookups (facilities, payment terms, categories) for the write bodies.

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Cost / analysis datasets — carrier invoices (FedEx, Veho) as pinned search columns + full raw rows. Per-carrier on purpose: zone/weight/charge semantics are not comparable across carriers.

tags.name: Legacy
tags.description: Endpoints backed by legacy data sources, published deliberately under a `legacy` name. They work and are safe to build on, but each will be superseded by a WMS-native replacement — expect a migration notice here when that happens.

bearerAuth.description: Per-app bearer token minted in the Tari console (System → API tokens). Scopes are listed per operation.

id.description: Facility id — pass as destination_facility_id on a PO / cargo load.

code.description: Payment term code — pass as payment_term_code on a PO.

anchor.description: Reference event the term counts from.

id.description: Category id — pass as category_id on an item.

level.description: Depth in the category tree (top level first).

parent_id.description: Parent category id; null at the top level.

sales_rank.description: Rank by 30-day online sold (1 = best seller).

parent_bundle_sku.description: Comma-separated bundle SKUs this item is a component of.

online_active_days_30d.description: Distinct days with at least one online sale in the last 30 days.

online_bundle_sold_5d.description: Subset of online_sold_5d that came through bundles — do NOT add to online_sold_5d.

committed_west.description: Shopify committed (unshipped order) units, West location.

incoming_local_po.description: Units on open local purchase orders (BoxHero in-progress/confirmed).

days_of_supply_online_west.description: (HQ West online stock − committed West) ÷ online_adj_daily. Null when velocity is 0; negative = oversold.

refreshed_at.description: When the underlying dataset was last refreshed (every 15 minutes).

reference_number.description: External / supplier PO number, when set.

status.description: e.g. draft, ordered, in_transit, received, closed.

order_date.description: Document / order date (ordered_at). Null on drafts never ordered.

expected_arrival.description: Latest linked inbound-shipment ETA, else the PO draft ETA.

total_amount.description: Goods value = Σ line qty × unit_cost. Excludes freight/customs charges.

created_by.description: public.users id of the creator (uuid). No name/email — PII minimized.

received_quantity.description: Best-effort receipts for this PO matched by item_id (approximate if the item spans multiple lines of one PO).

po_updated_at.description: Parent PO updated_at — the field updated_since filters on.

total_amount.description: Goods value = Σ line qty × unit_cost (Big.js).

ordered_at.description: Document / order date. Stamped automatically when status becomes ordered.

draft_inbound_eta.description: Expected arrival while the PO has no linked inbound shipment yet.

supplier_id.description: Vendor (supplier) id. REQUIRED unless `supplier_code` is sent. If both are sent they must resolve to the same active vendor (else 409).

supplier_code.description: Vendor code — the alternative to `supplier_id`. Case-insensitive (upper-cased before lookup); unique across active vendors.

item_id.description: WMS item id. REQUIRED unless `sku` is sent. If both are sent they must designate the same item (else 409).

sku.description: Item SKU — the alternative to `item_id`. Matched case-insensitively against active items; a SKU matching more than one active item returns 409 (send `item_id` instead).

vendor_sku.description: The supplier's own item code. Stored on the line and upserted onto the item↔vendor link — NOT a lookup key: it does not resolve the item.

barcode.description: Barcode recorded on the line (e.g. a catch-all MISC line). NOT a lookup key: it does not resolve the item.

lines.description: At least one line. Each line needs `item_id` or `sku`, plus `quantity` and `unit_cost`.

ordered_at.description: Document / order date. Stamped automatically when status becomes ordered.

draft_inbound_eta.description: Expected arrival while the PO has no linked inbound shipment yet.

item_id.description: WMS item id. REQUIRED unless `sku` is sent. If both are sent they must designate the same item (else 409).

sku.description: Item SKU — the alternative to `item_id`. Matched case-insensitively against active items; a SKU matching more than one active item returns 409 (send `item_id` instead).

vendor_sku.description: The supplier's own item code. Stored on the line and upserted onto the item↔vendor link — NOT a lookup key: it does not resolve the item.

barcode.description: Barcode recorded on the line (e.g. a catch-all MISC line). NOT a lookup key: it does not resolve the item.

lines.description: Declarative FULL REPLACE of the line set (matched by item — update in place, insert new, delete missing). Omit to leave lines untouched; when sent it must be non-empty.

container_number.description: Container number (ocean) or master AWB (air) — primary_identifier.

etd.description: Estimated departure (departure_estimated_time) — the schedule anchor + etd_from/etd_to filter target.

goods_total.description: Σ line qty × PO unit_cost, in the PO native currency (may mix currencies across POs).

created_by.description: public.users id of the creator (uuid). No name/email — PII minimized.

cargo_load_status.description: Status of the parent cargo load.

po_line_id.description: Linked PO line id (purchase_order_line_item_id), when PO-backed.

cargo_load_updated_at.description: Parent cargo load updated_at — the field updated_since filters on.

lot_slots.description: Split-expiry slots for this line (empty array when the line is not split). A split line carries its expiries here and its own `expiration_date` is null. Echo these back as `lots[]` when writing the line — a `lines` PATCH is a full replace and drops slots it is not given.

cargo_load_line_item_id.description: Set for line-level charges (e.g. customs duty on a specific line).

charge_category.description: Customs | Freight | Insurance | Tax | Service | Other.

affects_cost.description: Whether this charge rolls into landed cost.

id.description: PO line id — pass as po_line_id when composing a cargo load.

loaded_quantity.description: Quantity already loaded onto any cargo load.

remaining_quantity.description: ordered − loaded (> 0 for every returned row).

shelf_life_days.description: Item-master shelf life in days. Null means an expiry CANNOT be computed from a `production_date` — declare `expiration_date` on the cargo-load line instead.

shelf_life_basis.description: What `production_date` on a cargo-load line means for this item: manufacture_date | milling_date | packaging_date. Item-master value (shelf life is master data, not a per-order override).

goods_total.description: Goods value = Σ line qty × PO unit_cost (Big.js).

expiration_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Null on a split line — its expiries live in `lots`.

production_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD batch base date, when set.

lots.description: Split-expiry slots as persisted (empty when the line is not split). Echo these back on the next `lines` PATCH — a full replace without them deletes the slots.

expiration_date.description: Supplier-declared expiry for the whole line. Ignored when `lots[]` is present — a split line carries its expiries per slot and this field is nulled server-side.

production_date.description: Batch base date (manufacture / milling / packaging — which one is the item master’s `shelf_life_basis`, served on GET /cargo-loads/available-po-line-items). At receiving it anchors the COMPUTED expiry (production_date + the item’s `shelf_life_days`) when no expiry was declared. With no `shelf_life_days` on the item, nothing is computed.

external_lot_code.description: The supplier's / 3PL's lot code for the line, when known.

preliminary_expiry_date.description: Provisional expiry recorded pre-arrival (booking-time estimate). Informational — the expiry the LOT gets at receiving comes from `expiration_date` / the slots / the COMPUTED path, never from this field.

quantity.description: Units in this slot. The slots must sum to the line `quantity`.

expiration_date.description: Expiry for this slot — required (a slot exists to carry its own expiry).

external_lot_code.description: The supplier's / 3PL's lot code for this slot, when known.

lots.description: Split-expiry slots — one entry per expiry within this line. Sending a non-empty array puts the line in SPLIT mode: the line-level `expiration_date` is nulled and the truth lives in the slots. Their quantities must sum to the line `quantity`. A `lines` PATCH is a full replace, so omitting `lots` on a split line DELETES its slots — echo them back (they are returned on every write response).

lot_id.description: 0 means "no lot" — the lot_* fields are then null.

post.description: Create an item master record. Body is a restricted subset — cost/price, images, ingredients/allergens, customs/HS, sales-channel status, and external_id are console-only. Requires the `write:masters` scope and an `Idempotency-Key` header — replaying the same key returns 200 { noop: true }. A duplicate SKU or barcode returns 409. The response includes the generated display_name and barcode set.

schema.description: Unique key for this logical write. REQUIRED. Retrying with the same key never double-writes the ledger — the replay returns 200 { noop: true }.

200.description: Idempotent replay (same Idempotency-Key) — no new write happened.

schema.description: Idempotent replay — the same Idempotency-Key was already processed. No new document was created.

400.description: Validation error (bad body or missing Idempotency-Key).

403.description: Token missing the required scope (or has no owning user).

409.description: A SKU or barcode collision (an active item already uses this SKU, or the barcode is owned by another item).

patch.description: Update an item master record. Body is the same restricted subset, all fields optional. `sku` is IMMUTABLE — a body carrying a sku key returns 400. Requires the `write:masters` scope and an `Idempotency-Key` header — replaying the same key returns 200 { noop: true }. A missing or soft-deleted item returns 404; a barcode collision returns 409.

delete.description: Soft-delete an item (WOO-541) — equivalent to the internal delete: stamps deleted_at / deleted_by and, when the item carries an external_id, enqueues the one-way BoxHero delete (INV-018 — Tari never writes BoxHero directly). No request body. Requires the `write:masters` scope and an `Idempotency-Key` header. A missing OR already-deleted item returns 404 (delete is idempotent in effect — a replay hits the already-deleted row). Success → 200 { data: { deleted: true, id } }.

get.description:
SKU stock coverage — one row per inventoried SKU with 5/7/30-day sales per channel (online, retail POS stores, B2B), stock positions per location bucket, incoming quantities, and derived adjusted daily velocity + days-of-supply per channel. Backed by a materialized dataset refreshed every 15 minutes (`refreshed_at`).

⚠️ **Legacy inventory source**: stock positions are read from the legacy `inventory_levels` ledger — hence the endpoint name. When the WMS-native inventory (`wms_inventory_levels`) becomes authoritative, a replacement endpoint will be published and this one deprecated.

Transfer line items — one row per line with item, lot, per-line bins, and planned/picked/actual quantities. The grain a picking or receiving client works at. `updated_since` keys on the parent transfer’s updated_at.

**Auth axis**: `both` — will also accept a warehouse worker session (planned; machine tokens only today).

schema.description: Page size — default 100, max 500. Invalid values fall back to the default.
Keyset cursor from the previous page’s `next_cursor`.
ISO timestamp — return only lines whose parent transfer was updated at or after this time.
Exact parent transfer id.
Exact WMS item id.
Exact SKU.
Parent transfer status.
Line status, when tracked.

200.description: A page of transfer lines.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; null = last page.
